requirements.text: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin.
Deduplicate source revisions while retaining fetch provenance and parser version.
Recover partial runs without advancing progress past committed outputs.

problem.scope: Extend the synthetic collection exercise with scheduled run identity, origin politeness, deduplication and provenance. Inputs are authored URLs and synthetic records; no live crawler or extraction is claimed.

stages.explanation: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin. [A directed acyclic graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph) expresses work that depends on earlier results. A scheduler must track completed dependencies and distinguish logical tasks from retry attempts before releasing downstream work. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement. Retry the same source revision under a new lease.
invariants: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin.
stages.question: What does successful completion promise?
stages.reason: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin.
stages.title: Define the operation boundary

stages.explanation: Create one run per schedule/instant and admit only configured origins. Own normalized URL/revision keys, lease owner, attempts and next eligible time. run identity belongs to Run coordinator; URL leases belongs to Frontier. [A crawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler) chooses which URLs to fetch and when. Scheduling must balance discovery with per-site limits, while canonicalization and duplicate checks prevent repeated or unbounded work.
invariants: run identity belongs to Run coordinator; URL leases belongs to Frontier.
stages.question: Which component owns the decision and its persistent or shared state?
stages.reason: Create one run per schedule/instant and admit only configured origins. Own normalized URL/revision keys, lease owner, attempts and next eligible time.
stages.title: Expose authority and state

stages.explanation: Grant a bounded concurrent permit after robots and minimum-delay checks. Retries consume the same per-origin budget. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement. Retry the same source revision under a new lease.
invariants: Retries consume the same per-origin budget.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: How is one busy site protected?
stages.reason: Grant a bounded concurrent permit after robots and minimum-delay checks.
stages.title: Origin permit

stages.explanation: Use finite response-size/time limits and conditional validators; retain status and receipt. A timeout is retryable intent, not evidence of an empty source. [A condition variable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condition_variable) lets a thread sleep until shared state may have changed. Waking does not guarantee success, so the protected condition must be checked again. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: A timeout is retryable intent, not evidence of an empty source.
stages.question: What if a fetch times out?
stages.reason: Use finite response-size/time limits and conditional validators; retain status and receipt.
stages.title: Fetch executor

stages.explanation: Parse retained bytes with a pinned parser version and emit schema errors to quarantine. Invalid records never enter the accepted output table. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination. Stable source identity and progress records distinguish genuinely new data from repeated delivery or a restarted import. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: Invalid records never enter the accepted output table.
stages.question: Can a new parser reinterpret old content?
stages.reason: Parse retained bytes with a pinned parser version and emit schema errors to quarantine.
stages.title: Versioned parser

stages.explanation: Commit unique source/revision/parser outputs and completion marker atomically. The completion marker never outruns output commit. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement. Retry the same source revision under a new lease.
invariants: The completion marker never outruns output commit.
stages.question: When may the frontier advance?
stages.reason: Commit unique source/revision/parser outputs and completion marker atomically.
stages.title: Output transaction

stages.explanation: Fence expired lease holders and retry with the same run/revision identity. A stale worker cannot complete a reassigned lease. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: A stale worker cannot complete a reassigned lease.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: What if a worker dies mid-fetch?
stages.reason: Fence expired lease holders and retry with the same run/revision identity.
stages.title: Lease recovery

stages.explanation: Retain source URL, receipt hash, parser version, scheduled instant and terminal state. A record is attributable to immutable inputs. [Replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replication_%28computing%29) keeps copies of state on multiple nodes. Copying data alone does not decide which copy may accept writes or how much stale data a read may return. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: A record is attributable to immutable inputs.
stages.question: How is one record explained?
stages.reason: Retain source URL, receipt hash, parser version, scheduled instant and terminal state.
stages.title: Provenance index

tradeoffs: Frontier leases and per-origin queues add state.
Content changes need revision-aware deduplication rather than URL-only suppression.
